items.title: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by "all available means"
items.summary: Iran vows to force the U.S. to lift its blockade as Trump acknowledges the regime's increasing attacks, but says they've "done no damage."
items.t: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by "all available means"

items.title: From space, ‘you discover things hidden' back on Earth: Advancing research in health and medicine
items.summary: When kids look up into the night sky and marvel at the moon and the stars, the mysteries of space might spark their wondernment and curiosity. And one of France's most beloved astronauts, Thomas Pesquet, joins Eve Irvine to take us one step beyond with his new book "Space in 100 Questions", offering astronomy enthusiasts of all ages an otherworldly glimpse at the Final Frontier!
items.t: From space, ‘you discover things hidden' back on Earth: Advancing research in health and medicine

items.title: Russian drone violates Polish airspace days after cruise missiles fell on country – Europe live
items.summary:
Authorities investigating ‘intentional activity’ amid growing tensions between Moscow and countries on Nato’s eastern flank

The Slovakian parliament has approved contentious legislation to scrap postal voting for Slovaks living abroad – except for at Slovak embassies.

The bill passed by 79 votes to 71 in the 150-seat National Council, with lawmakers backing the ruling three-party coalition voting in favour of the legislation. The opposition is expected to challenge the measure in the country’s Constiutional Court if/when it is signed into law by Slovakia’s president, Peter Pellegrini.

Continue reading...
items.t: Russian drone violates Polish airspace days after cruise missiles fell on country – Europe live

items.title: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election
items.summary:
Exclusive: Ada Colau hopes public anger over housing will transfer into support for her Broad Front coalition in Sunday’s vote

The leader of Spain’s leftwing Broad Front coalition has called for a drastic rethink of the country’s entire housing rental system, and described the eviction of an 87-year-old woman – the spark for nationwide protests that in turn triggered Sunday’s snap general election – as “the last straw” for desperate tenants.

“We’re not interested in small changes,” Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor, told the Guardian in an interview. “We want to reform the entire rental sector.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election

items.title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention
items.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, drawing approval/plaudits/cheers  from Wall Street and criticism from US lawmakers. The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
items.t: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention

items.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct
items.summary:
President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

(Image credit: Angela Weiss)
items.t: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct

items.title: Macron mulls enshrining fiscal rules in French constitution
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has suggested reviving a 15-year-old proposal to enshrine a framework for public finances in the constitution, as a possible response to concerns in financial markets over France's fiscal trajectory. "If there is still volatility by January, thinking about a 'golden rule' of the type proposed in 2011 could be an idea worth exploring," Macron said, speaking to Le Figaro.
items.t: Macron mulls enshrining fiscal rules in French constitution

items.title: French chefs battle it out at Paris egg mayo championships
items.summary: It is one of the most common starters in the French culinary repertoire, but the humble egg mayonnaise is also a test of any chef's prowess. The World Egg Mayonnaise Championship this week brought together cooks from across France and beyond to find out who makes the best.
items.t: French chefs battle it out at Paris egg mayo championships

items.title: Istanbul lioness never existed, Turkish officials say after search
items.summary: A 24-hour search for a lioness in the Istanbul suburbs that sparked panic among local residents was thrown into fresh confusion late Monday when Turkish officials said the animal didn't exist.
items.t: Istanbul lioness never existed, Turkish officials say after search

items.title: Simple Minds at 50: Still alive and kicking
items.summary: From Glasgow teenagers to global rock stars, Simple Minds have spent nearly five decades filling stadiums and creating some of the defining songs of their generation. Now, as the band celebrate 50 years with new music "Sacrosanct" and a major 2027 tour, Jim Kerr tells Eve Jackson about the music, the memories and the moments that shaped Simple Minds, including the night he discovered they were number one in America by telegram in a hotel in Nice.
items.t: Simple Minds at 50: Still alive and kicking

items.title: 'Nothing will ever be the same' for Jensen Huang and Nvidia after his return
items.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 24: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia dominates the papers. In other news, leaked records shed new light on Russian military losses in Ukraine. Also, the UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup. Finally, a devilled eggs world championship crowns its winner.
items.t: 'Nothing will ever be the same' for Jensen Huang and Nvidia after his return

items.title: Man with Alzheimer's found alive after 11 days lost in jungle
items.summary: Rescue workers said the man survived in the jungle by eating berries, drinking water from natural sources and making bedlike structures with the leaves of acai palms.
items.t: Man with Alzheimer's found alive after 11 days lost in jungle

items.title: AFCON: Ten months on, court to rule on 2025 winner
items.summary: Ten months after the Africa Cup of Nations final was chaotically played on the field between Morocco and Senegal, the title will be awarded Tuesday by sports’ highest court. The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the target Monday to publish the verdict of its panel of three judges on Senegal’s appeal to regain the title the team won on the field in Morocco in January and then lost in a legal case in March.
items.t: AFCON: Ten months on, court to rule on 2025 winner

items.title: ICE raids add to jitters ahead of Thanksgiving travel rush
items.summary: Travellers in the US are heading into a particularly stressful holiday travel period this week. Recent network outages for US airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration have raised concerns about flight delays and cancellations ahead of Thanksgiving on Thursday. This, plus ICE agents ramping up arrests at airports, has made many travellers anxious.
items.t: ICE raids add to jitters ahead of Thanksgiving travel rush

items.title: Researcher who helped improve melanoma survival rates among winners of top Australian science prize
items.summary:
Georgina Long and subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas recognised in Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

When Prof Georgina Long was starting out in melanoma treatment and research, “my waiting room would change so rapidly”.

Referring to her patients with stage 4 melanoma, the oncologist and medical director at the Melanoma Institute Australia said she wouldn’t “see the same face for more than nine months, 12 months maximum”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Researcher who helped improve melanoma survival rates among winners of top Australian science prize

items.title: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
items.summary:
Temporary quotas on vehicles entering the bloc tariff-free will also apply to cars from the UK, Japan and Turkey

  • Business live – latest updates

The EU will next month impose its threatened caps on the number of Chinese hybrid cars that can be imported into the bloc without facing a tariff, the European Commission has announced.

The quotas will also apply to hybrids from Japan, Turkey, South Korea and the UK, but the principal purpose is to limit imports from China after an agreement with Beijing in October that has led to a rise in exports to the bloc.

Continue reading...
items.t: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month

items.title: How the AI trade could trap even cautious investors
items.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.
items.t: How the AI trade could trap even cautious investors

items.title: Thousands evacuated from UK concert after release of 'unknown substance'
items.summary: British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from ​a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital. Police ​declared ‌a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the ⁠Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during ‌a performance by US rapper Don Toliver.
items.t: Thousands evacuated from UK concert after release of 'unknown substance'

items.title: Spain set to head to polls in snap election that could boost far right
items.summary: Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to thwart grim polls as polarised Spain holds an election on Sunday that could propel the opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) and the far right to power. The outcome will be closely watched across Europe as it opens a cycle of elections over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the European Union.
items.t: Spain set to head to polls in snap election that could boost far right

items.title: Is Russia preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite?
items.summary: German media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, have claimed that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. In response, NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space. France 24’s correspondent in Berlin Nick Holdsworth has the details.
items.t: Is Russia preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite?

items.title: Republicans, Democrats unite in anger over Trump's Nvidia intervention
items.summary: Members of Congress responded with swift, bipartisan fury Monday over the Nvidia board's surprise decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang at the behest of US President Donald Trump, opening a new phase of questions about the chipmaking giant and potential national security lapses. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.
items.t: Republicans, Democrats unite in anger over Trump's Nvidia intervention

items.title: Nvidia's position as cornerstone of AI trade confirmed by market reaction to Huang's return
items.summary: Tech shares in Asia and Europe rebounded on Tuesday, following in the footsteps of Nvidia's shares closing on Wall Street 31 percent higher on Monday. The return of CEO Jensen Huang, 11 days after his resignation over an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, has reassured investors in the AI trade. In this edition, we look at Nvidia's central role in this trade, and Huang's central role at Nvidia. Also, French President Emmanuel Macron proposes to enshrine fiscal rules in the constitution.
items.t: Nvidia's position as cornerstone of AI trade confirmed by market reaction to Huang's return

items.title: Accused of ‘emptying the coffers’, Macron mulls spending caps for future French governments
items.summary: Right-wing candidates vying to succeed French President Emmanuel Macron have welcomed his suggestion of a “golden rule” to cap government spending and keep deficits in check, even as they mock the profligacy of his decade in power. Critics of the proposal denounce a budgetary straitjacket imposed on future governments and a distraction from the president’s growing impotence at home.
items.t: Accused of ‘emptying the coffers’, Macron mulls spending caps for future French governments

items.title: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution
items.summary:
A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

(Image credit: Marie Ruwet)
items.t: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution

items.title: Death of Nahel: French police officer who shot dead a teenage boy to stand trial for murder
items.summary: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by the Versailles appeals court. Merzouk's death at the hands of the police sparked intense riots in the sprawling suburbs surrounding Paris.
items.t: Death of Nahel: French police officer who shot dead a teenage boy to stand trial for murder

items.title: Fighting between Russia and Ukraine has expanded geographically, drawing concerns
items.summary: In recent days, Ukraine has sunk a Russian warship docked in port in Libya, and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. The Kremlin has not commented on the missiles.
items.t: Fighting between Russia and Ukraine has expanded geographically, drawing concerns

items.title: Pope Francis had visions of devil, "gates of hell," diary reveals
items.summary: Pope Francis suffered a profound spiritual crisis in 2021-2022 linked to temptations to exercise power omnipotently, his diary reveals, adding that he overcame it by entrusting himself entirely to God's mercy.
items.t: Pope Francis had visions of devil, "gates of hell," diary reveals

items.title: China to launch first space mission with a foreign astronaut
items.summary: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.
items.t: China to launch first space mission with a foreign astronaut

items.title: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws
items.summary:
Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech firms for harm suffered online under compromise deal

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Big tech companies may face “multibillion-dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court under Australia’s new digital duty of care laws, with the Greens to support the bill’s passage after extracting major amendments from Labor.

From late 2027, Australians will also be able opt out of addictive online algorithms under the new legislation, while the “endless scroll” of social media feeds may also cease.
items.t: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws

items.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
items.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.
items.t: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?

items.title: ICG: "It's hard to imagine" Tripoli would risk its ties with Russia by approving a Ukrainian attack
items.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Claudia Gazzini, International Crisis Group's Senior Analyst for Libya. The Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship off the coast of eastern Libya has raised questions about Russian and Ukrainian military activity in the country. Gazzini discusses Russia's established military presence in eastern Libya and allegations that Ukrainian forces are operating in the west. She notes that while Russia is militarily present in eastern Libya, it also maintains "good commercial ties and political ties with western authorities as well." For Gazzini, the suggestion that Tripoli would approve such an operation "just sounds a bit too hazardous."
items.t: ICG: "It's hard to imagine" Tripoli would risk its ties with Russia by approving a Ukrainian attack

items.title: Campaigners urge Albanese government to reject ‘climate bomb’ coalmine expansion after Cop31
items.summary:
Hunter Valley Operations expansion in New South Wales would allow additional 430m tonnes of coal to be extracted and burned

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Climate campaigners are urging the Albanese government to heed a “line in the sand” warning on fossil fuels issued by dozens of countries at a UN climate summit and refuse a massive coalmine expansion planned in New South Wales.

A proposed agreement at the Cop31 negotiations in Turkey failed after a list of nations – including European Union members, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway and Belize – said they would not support it unless it included an explicit statement that the world needed to transition away from fossil fuels.

Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter

items.title: ‘State-sanctioned theft’: Australian news outlets demand content is protected from AI scraping – as it happened
items.summary:
• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The government will save more than it spends, says Jim Chalmers, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.

Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).

There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.

We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.

You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. I think it’s a bit of a symbol of the quite extraordinary volatility, unpredictability that we’re seeing play out in markets in the AI sector, but more broadly as well.
items.t: Australian politics live: Penny Wong to defend US alliance; rental affordability plummets to 14-year low

items.summary: Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO pushed the AI computing company's stocks up more than 30 percent Monday. But the model of circular financing increasingly underwriting the AI boom still has some analysts worried that the party can't last forever.

items.title: Collapse of COP31: 'This deal was a bad deal and better no deal than a bad deal'
items.summary: François Picard is joined by Ireland's former environment minister Eamon Ryan following the collapse of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. "Political science trumps climate science still," Ryan reacted. The talks failed after the European Union and up to 100 countries refused to accept a final text that abandoned earlier commitments to transition away from fossil fuels.

items.title: AFCON 2025: CAS set to hand down ruling on controversial final
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will deliver its ruling this Tuesday on the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final. Senegal won the match on the pitch, but Morocco were awarded the trophy following an appeal to the CAF.

items.title: Sports whistleblowers protected under proposed laws amid Australian cricket ball tampering saga
items.summary:
Amendments to government bill by Coalition and Greens would establish protections for those reporting wrongdoing in sport

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Whistleblowers reporting corruption or misconduct in sport would be protected under draft laws put forward by the Coalition and the Greens, in response to the Australian Test cricket ball-tampering scandal.

The South Africa tour of 2018 is back in the national spotlight after the publication of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography earlier this month, in which he claimed players had used sandpaper to tamper with the ball before the third Test on the infamous tour, and that the entire squad knew about the practice.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

items.title: Malaysia to send thousands of migrants back to Myanmar as PM acknowledges junta’s ‘atrocities’
items.summary:
Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement comes days after the ICJ found Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya minority

Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging that many asylum seekers in the country had been victims of “atrocities” carried ​out by the junta in Naypyidaw.

The announcement comes just days after the UN’s highest court ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

Continue reading...

items.title: Live: Russian strikes on Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia kill two people and wound dozens more
items.summary: A Russian attack killed two people in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia overnight, regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Tuesday. Some 40 people, four of them children, were also wounded in the strikes, the governor added. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.
items.t: Live: Tripoli demands explanation from Kyiv for striking Russian ships in Libyan waters

items.title: Ebikes, screens and failing manners pose challenge for Dutch cycling culture
items.summary:
Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads

For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80.

In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ebikes, screens and failing manners pose challenge for Dutch cycling culture

items.title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter after Russian military aircraft approach
items.summary:
The order was issued after aircraft entered the country’s air defence identification zone over the island of Ulleungdo

Residents of a remote South Korean island were ordered to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft came close to entering its airspace, prompting a pre-emptive alert from the military that anticipated a violation.

The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché on Tuesday afternoon to lodge a strong protest.

Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, said the convicted person was surnamed Ma and was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.

items.summary:
Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday.

With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.

items.title: Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ to rejoin EU without referendum
items.summary:
Prime minister also says former Tory premiers who have criticised revival of Brexit debate are ‘stuck in the past’

Andy Burnham has said it would be “unthinkable” for the UK to rejoin the EU without holding another referendum, offering his strongest commitment yet to directly consulting the public if he concludes Britain should go back in.

The prime minister is planning to set out the long-term options for closer ties with the bloc next month, with concrete steps coming after the next general election, as he has pledged to stick to Labour’s manifesto red lines.

items.summary: Dwain Hall was found guilty of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby, and was sentenced to two consecutive life terms, Florida prosecutors said.

items.summary:
Island’s labour minister, Colin Jordan, says agreement acknowledges links between Speightstown and UK city are rooted in slave trade

A town in Barbados known as “Little Bristol” has signed a “twinning’” agreement with the UK city, marking a new chapter in a centuries-long relationship rooted in the transatlantic slave trade.

Barbados says the new partnership between Speightstown and Bristol is part of its wider push for reparatory justice, built in small steps rather than around a multi-trillion-pound claim.

Delegation of 50 to accompany minister, with trip criticised after universities were warned about Chinese interference

The education secretary, Lucy Powell, is travelling to Beijing this week to promote UK education, weeks after MI5 issued a rare public warning to universities about Chinese interference in UK academia.

A 50-strong UK delegation, including 18 university leaders, will accompany the minister when she attends the first UK-China education summit in nine years, aimed at opening up new opportunities for universities, colleges and education businesses.

items.title: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
items.summary:
New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people

• Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
items.t: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
